first_five_minutes:
Cassy lands on Mission Control and it is beautiful and legible: DEMO badges on every synthetic number, "Not running. Not pretending to." on the specialists card, a footer that tells her exactly where her changes live. She opens Cassandra's Desk, types an idea, and sees "Not saved yet · Kept in this tab until you save" — which is true there, and it is the single best thing in this build. She reloads on purpose to test it; her words survive. Good.

Then she wanders. She opens a brief, hits Edit, rewrites the middle paragraph, cancels the dialog — the card warns her she has unsaved edits and offers "Continue editing." Excellent. But she then clicks Approve, because she thinks approving is what saves it; the dialog says the decision is final and mentions nothing about her rewrite, and after "Confirm approval" her edited text is gone (approval-card.tsx:67 clears the edit draft, and the brief that got approved is the old draft). She has no idea it happened.

On the connected side she opens Assassin's Refusal, clicks "Edit book details," writes four paragraphs of her own book description into the dialog, gets distracted, and presses Escape. Nothing warns her; nothing was kept. On Marketing Plans she fills the whole form — name, intent, books, goals — and reads "Not saved yet · Kept in this tab until you save." That sentence is false there: the value lives in a component useState (plans-page.tsx:68), so a reload, a stray navigation, or an expired session takes all of it, and neither the beforeunload guard nor the sign-out dialog counts it as unsaved work. Same for a long Teach Raven lesson. She alt-tabs to check something, comes back, the focus listener refreshes, the session has expired, and because none of those fields register as "private drafts" the app hard-redirects her to /login with no dialog and no copy button.

By minute five the app has earned a lot of trust with its language and then quietly broken the specific promise that language made. For someone who has lost 40,000 words once, that is worse than never making the promise.

scores.verdict: Consent and role gating are genuinely good — permission is asked before the manuscript is read, spoilers are off by default, reading can be paused, every 'replace my draft' moment gives her the keep option. But on her most intimate asset she has no exit: she cannot delete her manuscript, cannot download it back, and cannot see who granted permission or how big the file was. The copy points her at the workspace owner for removal, and the owner has no path either.

top_findings.title: Approving a brief silently destroys her unsaved rewrite of it
top_findings.problem: After a successful approve or reject, clearEditDrafts(approval.id) deletes the kept edit text. The confirm dialog (line 214) never mentions that unsaved edits exist or that they will be dropped, and the decision is recorded against approval.draft — the version she was in the middle of replacing. Once status leaves 'pending' the unsaved-edits notice at line 152 stops rendering, so there is no trace it ever existed.
top_findings.proposed_change: When keptEditFor returns a non-null unsaved edit and the modal is approve/reject, extend the dialog description with 'You have unsaved edits to this brief. Approving records Draft N as saved and discards them.' and add a 'Save my draft first' action that runs the edit transition before the decision.

top_findings.title: Marketing Plans claims draft protection it does not have
top_findings.problem: PlanForm renders 'Not saved yet · Kept in this tab until you save' — the exact wording used by the genuinely sessionStorage-backed desk scratchpad — while its value lives in a component useState at line 68. A reload, a navigation, an error boundary, or an expired session loses the whole form. Because the value is not in the store, hasPrivateDrafts (demo-store.tsx:154) does not see it, so beforeunload does not warn, the sign-out dialog does not warn, and the session-ended dialog cannot hand it back.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add a planScratchpad to the private scratchpads in lib/db/demo-store.tsx (same schema-validated sessionStorage path as studioScratchpad) and drive PlanForm from it; if that is out of scope tonight, change line 88 to 'Not saved yet · This form clears if you reload or leave the page.'

top_findings.title: Session expiry discards unprotected long-text fields with no dialog
top_findings.problem: endSession() only stops to hand words back when hasPrivateDrafts is true (line 154), which covers just the desk scratchpad, Learn blueprints, Ask Raven prompt and brief edits. The Teach Raven lesson (approval-card.tsx:35), BookMetadataForm fields, PlanForm, plan review notes, plan result notes and the NotebookLM box are all plain component state. A 401 arriving from the window-focus refresh (demo-store.tsx:592) therefore calls window.location.replace('/login') immediately and takes all of them.
top_findings.proposed_change: Give the store a registerDraft(key, label, getText) API, have every long-text field register, and include registered drafts in hasPrivateDrafts so beforeunload, the sign-out confirm and the session-ended dialog all cover them.

top_findings.title: Unreadable stored drafts and failed draft writes are both swallowed in silence
top_findings.problem: restoreDrafts returns a fresh scratchpad whenever the stored JSON fails schema validation, discarding exactly the unsaved words the mechanism exists to protect — the comment even argues 'nothing she saved lives here', which is backwards. persistDrafts (line 99) likewise swallows quota or private-mode write failures while the UI keeps printing 'Kept in this tab until you save.' Compare the care taken with corruptWorkspace, which preserves the raw file and offers a download.
top_findings.proposed_change: Preserve the raw string on a parse failure and surface it through the same dialog pattern as corruptWorkspace; on a persist failure set a store flag and show 'This browser could not hold your draft — copy it before reloading' next to the save-state line.

top_findings.title: A stale pending Ask Raven request locks the question form permanently
top_findings.problem: busy is derived from studioScratchpad.pendingRequestId, which is persisted to sessionStorage (demo-store.tsx:70). finishStudioRequest only runs in the ask() finally block, so a tab closed or crashed mid-request leaves the flag set. On return to /studio the submit button reads 'Raven is thinking…' and is disabled forever, and the only reset (startNewQuestion, line 147) is rendered solely inside a generation card. book-knowledge.tsx:64 also treats it as 'unfinished or running' and refuses to open Raven.
top_findings.proposed_change: Clear pendingRequestId on mount (or treat a restored one as stale and show 'Your last question may not have been sent — check recent questions'), and render the reset control on the bare /studio form as well.

top_findings.title: Book description and Add-book dialogs discard typed prose on Escape
top_findings.problem: The Edit book details dialog uses onOpenChange={setEditing} with uncontrolled defaultValue fields (connected-library.tsx:42-53), including a 10,000-character 'Author-approved description'. Escape or an outside click closes it and the text is gone; nothing warns, nothing is kept, and the field is invisible to the draft guard. Same for the Add book dialog at connected-library.tsx:76.
top_findings.proposed_change: Track dirtiness in BookMetadataForm and intercept onOpenChange when dirty, showing the same keep/discard choice used by the sign-out and new-question dialogs.

top_findings.title: A failed Marketing Plans load renders as an empty plan list
top_findings.problem: The 'Your plans' card renders 'Your first plan starts below' whenever plans.length === 0, regardless of loaded/error. cmobile-plans.png shows the error banner and that sentence on screen together, which reads to a user as 'your plans are gone.'
top_findings.proposed_change: Gate the empty state on loaded && !error; when the load failed, say 'We could not read your plan list. This is not an empty list.' with a retry.

top_findings.title: Her manuscript can never be removed or retrieved, and the copy names a rescuer who cannot help
top_findings.problem: Storage policy kira_manuscript_no_delete (supabase/migrations/202609190001_manuscript_intelligence.sql:473) blocks delete for every authenticated role, and there is no download route under app/api/manuscripts. The UI tells her to 'ask your workspace owner if you need a file removed', but the owner has no in-app path either. The custody list also withholds the file size and the consenting member it says it recorded (line 171).
top_findings.proposed_change: Add a signed-URL download per version; state plainly that no one can remove a manuscript from inside the app yet; show the recorded size and permission grantor. Whether an author-initiated withdrawal exists at all is an owner decision that also needs SQL work.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Does an author-initiated manuscript withdrawal exist? If yes it needs a soft-withdraw status, chunk/embedding purge and a server-only capability; if no, the permanence must be stated at the moment of upload.

top_findings.title: Two destructive connection actions have no confirmation
top_findings.problem: The Remove button on a saved link deletes it on a single click with no dialog and no undo, and 'Disconnect Meta' (line 125) revokes provider authorization the same way — requiring the whole hosted consent flow to redo. Every other destructive action in the app (reset demo, remove access, sign out with drafts, discard question) is confirmed with the safe option focused.
top_findings.proposed_change: Reuse the Remove access dialog pattern for both, with 'Keep' focused and the destructive button styled variant="destructive".

top_findings.title: The export is presented as a safety net but cannot be restored, and the error boundary over-promises
top_findings.problem: 'Export them before switching devices or clearing site data' frames the JSON as a backup, while the fact that it 'cannot be loaded back into KIRA OS' appears only inside the reset-confirm dialog at line 171. Separately app/error.tsx:226 states 'Nothing you saved has been lost' unconditionally, including when the error fired during a save.
top_findings.proposed_change: Put the no-reimport sentence next to the export button in Settings and on the desk's Export decisions control; soften error.tsx to 'Anything you had already saved is untouched. Unsaved text in the page you were on may not have survived.'

what_works: The desk scratchpad is the real thing, not a gesture: schema-validated sessionStorage per mode and per signed-in account (lib/db/demo-store.tsx:74), a keyed provider so a different account cannot inherit in-memory notes (line 567), and an honest inline save state at manual-review-form.tsx:248.

SessionEndedDialog is the best draft-loss handling I have reviewed in this kind of app — an expired session stops, lists every unfinished piece with a per-item Copy button in a read-only textarea, refuses Escape and outside-click, and only clears after she chooses to leave (session-ended-dialog.tsx:75-111).

The unreadable-demo-file path keeps her old localStorage payload byte-for-byte, refuses to write over it (demo-store.tsx:213), and offers 'Download the unreadable workspace file' before 'Start a fresh demo workspace'. That is exactly the behaviour I wanted and almost never see.

Sign-out with unsaved work opens a confirm whose safe option ('Keep working') is the one that receives focus, with the destructive button labelled 'Sign out and discard drafts' rather than a euphemism (app-shell.tsx:470-482).

Edited briefs are keyed to the draft number they were written against, so a concurrent change surfaces 'You wrote them against Draft 2; this brief is now Draft 3' and blocks the save instead of silently clobbering (approval-card.tsx:156, demo-store.tsx:135).

Every replace-my-words moment asks first: the idea shelf prefill (manual-review-form.tsx:134), the book-details starter (book-detail.tsx:215), the Learn shareable starter (learn-page.tsx:158), and starting a new Raven question (studio-page.tsx:215).

Error copy consistently tells her where her words are — 'Your text is still here; please try again', 'Your blueprint is still here; try again or download a copy', 'Your unfinished notes are still here' — rather than apologising without information.

Manuscript handling is honest and staged: an explicit permission checkbox, a four-bullet 'What happens to your file' that names the providers and the other people who can read it, storage separated from reading, a pausable background job with saved progress, and findings that omit any quotation that cannot be matched to the source (connected-book-detail.tsx:143-162).

Approve/reject confirmations state finality in plain words and explicitly bound the consequence — 'Nothing will be published, sent, purchased, or changed outside this workspace' (approval-card.tsx:214) — and the desk repeats it as a standing notice.
Connected-mode export copy lists what the file does not contain (settings-page.tsx:133) instead of implying completeness, and Teach Raven notices say 'No model was retrained' (demo-store.tsx:437).
